newsitem.title: MALTA: Bank shares up on Malta exchange.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares up on Malta exchange.

text.p: Bank shares gained at the once weekly trading session of the Malta stock exchange on Wednesday but shares in Suncrest hotels lost an average of five cents in their third week of trading.
Turnover in the trading session dropped to 1.6 million Maltese pounds ($4.16 million) after a record of 4.2 million pounds the previous week as the government issued new bonds.
Trading in government bonds continued to dominate trading on Wednesday, accounting for 1.4 million pounds of total turnover.
In equities, trading in Mid-Med Bank was especially active, with 43,613 shares changing hands in 14 deals for an average 158 cents per share, up three cents.
There were 44 deals in Bank of Valletta with 26,529 shares selling for an average 127 cents each, up by one cent.
Lombard Bank Malta shares gained two cents, with 5,000 shares selling for an average 145 cents.
Middle Sea Insurance shares gained one cent, with 1,245 shares selling for an average 123 cents per share.
There was no trading in Simonds Farsons Cisk, but ordinary shares in Suncrest Hotels lost five cents, with 3,100 shares selling for 70 cents per share.
The share index gained 3.52 to reach 1,003.59.

In corporate bonds, there were three deals in 6.5 percent Gasan bonds 1998/99 at an average price of 99 cents, unchanged and eight deals in 8.25 percent Suncrest Bonds 2005/7 amounting to 100.1 cents, down 0.1 cents. ($1=38 cents)
